sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vivek Tripathi,Satendra Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
1.
List revised.
Supplementary affidavit filed by Sri Satendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, today in the Court is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasia, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. As per prosecution version, the marriage of the daughter of the informant was solemnised with the applicant on 20.04.2016, after the marriage her in-laws including the applicant used to quarrel with regard to the dowry amount given in the marriage due to which, she was abused, beaten and on several occasion they tried to kill her by sprinkling the kerosene oil upon her and with regard to the said incident, earlier complaints were also made before the concerned Police Station.
On 10.08.2022 at about 05:00 P.M. her daughter was murdered and without informing him, her cremation was also done in his absence to vanish the evidence.

Satish Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24802135/
1 3.

entities.text: Satish Mishra vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The applicant never demanded dowry or did he torture the deceased.
The applicant is bereaved by the death of his wife and prays for peace of the departed soul.
However, for the purpose of the bail application, it is submitted that the deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions even on trivial issues.
The applicant did not abet or instigate the deceased to commit the suicide.

Learned counsel further submits that prior to the incident, the son of the deceased aged about five years was died in an accident in the month of June 2022 on account of which, the deceased was living under depression and had made attempt to commit suicide and lastly she was succeeded on 10.08.2022 in committing suicide.

Learned counsel further submits that when the parents of the applicant were in jail, the minor daughter of the applicant was looked after by his relative as has been stated in paragraph no.9 of the supplementary affidavit dated 06.02.2024 and since the parents of the applicant are old aged person, thus the minor daughter of the applicant could not be properly looked after by them.

He next submits that though the charge sheet was submitted long back and the trial too had commenced as S.C. No. 36 of 2023 (State Vs. Satish and others) in which charges were framed on 31.01.2023 but till date not even a single witness has been examined and that the trial is not likely to be concluded in near future.

entities.text: S.C. No. 36 of 2023 (State Vs. Satish and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been mentioned.

It has also been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.

He lastly submits that the mother-in-law namely, Smt. Manju Mishra and father-in-law namely Bhriguram Mishra have already been enlarged on bail by this Court as well as by co-ordinate Bench vide order dated 28.04.2023 and 12.05.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 57754 of 2022 and 59920 of 2022 copy of which orders have been annexed as collectively as Annexure-6 to the affidavit accompanying the bail application.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 57754 of 2022 and 59920 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He next submits that applicant is languishing in jail since 10.08.2022 having no criminal history.

4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the innocence of the applicant cannot be adjudged at pre trial stage, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence.
In case the applicant is released on bail he will misuse the liberty of bail.

5. Perusal of the record shows that there is specific averments in the F.I.R. that the deceased was earlier tried to be killed by sprinkling the kerosene oil upon her, with regard to same, complaints were made.
On 10.08.2022, she was murdered and her cremation was also done in the absence of the informant and his family members.
The statements of the informant as well as his wife recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. as well as other witnesses are intact.

So far the arguments of learned counsel for the applicant that the charges were framed on 31.01.2023 and till date no witness has been examined is concerned, perusal of the order sheets of the case shows that the Court was vacant for a considerable period.

The bailed out accused persons i.e. the mother and father in law of the deceased, out of which, one appeared before the trial Court and the other filed exemption application, which continues for long time.

For the first time, the informant was summoned vide order dated 06.12.2023 fixing the matter for 18.12.2023 and on 18.12.2023 the date was fixed for Satish Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24802135/
2 10.01.2024.

entities.text: Satish Mishra vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Order sheets of the aforesaid trial, after 18.12.2023 has not been annexed, copy of order sheets of the case is annexed as Annexure-SA1 to the supplementary affidavit.
Thus the arguments of learned counsel for the applicant that the trial is not likely to be concluded in near future has no legs.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the bail application moved on behalf of the applicant Satish Mishra for enlarging him on bail in Case Crime No.141 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 304B, 504, 323, 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Bariyarpur, District Deoria, is liable to be rejected.
7. Accordingly, it is rejected.
